symbols.name: matrix P
symbols.meaning: A matrix, the first factor of a tensor product.
symbols.quote: Let $P$ be a matrix, with row index $\xi$ and column index $\sigma$, so $p_{\xi\sigma}$ is its entry in row $\xi$ and column $\sigma$.

symbols.name: entry of P
symbols.meaning: The entry of $P$ in row $\xi$ and column $\sigma$.
symbols.quote: Let $P$ be a matrix, with row index $\xi$ and column index $\sigma$, so $p_{\xi\sigma}$ is its entry in row $\xi$ and column $\sigma$.

symbols.name: matrix Q
symbols.meaning: A second matrix, the second factor of a tensor product.
symbols.quote: Let $Q$ be a second matrix, with row index $\upsilon$ and column index $\zeta$, so $q_{\upsilon\zeta}$ is its entry in row $\upsilon$ and column $\zeta$.

symbols.name: entry of Q
symbols.meaning: The entry of $Q$ in row $\upsilon$ and column $\zeta$.
symbols.quote: Let $Q$ be a second matrix, with row index $\upsilon$ and column index $\zeta$, so $q_{\upsilon\zeta}$ is its entry in row $\upsilon$ and column $\zeta$.

symbols.name: row index
symbols.meaning: A row index of $P$, and in an address the output bit string $\xi$.
symbols.quote: Let $P$ be a matrix, with row index $\xi$ and column index $\sigma$, so $p_{\xi\sigma}$ is its entry in row $\xi$ and column $\sigma$.

symbols.name: column index
symbols.meaning: A column index of $P$, and in an address the input bit string $\sigma$.
symbols.quote: Let $P$ be a matrix, with row index $\xi$ and column index $\sigma$, so $p_{\xi\sigma}$ is its entry in row $\xi$ and column $\sigma$.

symbols.name: row index of Q
symbols.quote: Let $Q$ be a second matrix, with row index $\upsilon$ and column index $\zeta$, so $q_{\upsilon\zeta}$ is its entry in row $\upsilon$ and column $\zeta$.

symbols.name: column index of Q
symbols.quote: Let $Q$ be a second matrix, with row index $\upsilon$ and column index $\zeta$, so $q_{\upsilon\zeta}$ is its entry in row $\upsilon$ and column $\zeta$.

symbols.name: factor count
symbols.meaning: The number of factors in a tensor power, which is also the number of coordinates it acts on.
symbols.quote: Its $J$-fold power, where $J$ is the number of factors, applies one operator to $J$ coordinates at once, which is the step the [Simultaneous butterfly layer](simultaneous-butterfly-layer.md) relies on.

symbols.name: address bit
symbols.meaning: The bit of an input address $\sigma$ at coordinate $l$.
symbols.quote: Here an address on $J$ coordinates is a bit string $\sigma=(\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_J)\in\{0,1\}^J$ whose bit at coordinate $l$ is $\sigma_l$, with $l$ running from $1$ to $J$, and $\xi=(\xi_1,\dots,\xi_J)$ is an output address of the same form.

symbols.name: coordinate index
symbols.meaning: The index of a coordinate, running from $1$ to $J$.
symbols.quote: Here an address on $J$ coordinates is a bit string $\sigma=(\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_J)\in\{0,1\}^J$ whose bit at coordinate $l$ is $\sigma_l$, with $l$ running from $1$ to $J$, and $\xi=(\xi_1,\dots,\xi_J)$ is an output address of the same form.

symbols.name: function on addresses
symbols.meaning: A complex-valued function on addresses of $J$ bits, which $P^{\otimes J}$ transforms.

symbols.name: single-coordinate operator
symbols.meaning: The operator that applies $P$ to coordinate $l$ and the identity to the other coordinates.
symbols.quote: Let $P_{(l)}$ apply $P$ to coordinate $l$ and the identity to the others, so $P_{(l)}=I\otimes\cdots\otimes P\otimes\cdots\otimes I$ with $P$ in place $l$.

relations.quote: The tensor product is built from matrices, the basic objects of [Linear algebra basics](linear-algebra-basics.md).
The tensor product takes its one-coordinate factor from the [Butterfly](butterfly.md) map $H_0$, which replaces a pair of values by its half-sum and half-difference.
